cards.headline: PM Modi opens first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi
cards.body: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Purana Qila in New Delhi. Speaking at the event, he said cultural engagement is the strongest guarantee of global peace at a time when war and unrest dominate world discussions. The forum coincides with the SCO's 25th anniversary and growing cooperation in security, economy and connectivity.
cards.why_it_matters: It introduces a new India-hosted SCO platform that brings member countries together on culture and people-to-people ties rather than only security and trade.
cards.key_fact: First SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum held at Purana Qila, Delhi

quiz.q: Where was the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum inaugurated?
quiz.explain: The article states PM Modi inaugurated the forum at Purana Qila in New Delhi.

cards.headline: India, Netherlands sign 17 MoUs, upgrade ties to Strategic Partnership
cards.body: During PM Narendra Modi's visit to the Netherlands on May 16-17, 2026, the two countries upgraded ties to a Strategic Partnership and signed 17 agreements and MoUs. Areas covered include water, agriculture and health (WAH), renewable energy, critical minerals, and a semiconductor fabrication project between TATA Electronics and Dutch firm ASML. Dutch PM Rob Jetten said he also raised sensitive topics, which the MEA pushed back on.
cards.why_it_matters: The semiconductor tie-up and critical minerals deals matter for India's technology supply chains and its push to become a chip-making hub.
cards.key_fact: 17 agreements and MoUs signed during India-Netherlands Strategic Partnership

quiz.q: How many agreements and MoUs did India and the Netherlands sign during PM Modi's visit?
quiz.explain: The article says the two sides signed 17 agreements and memorandums of understanding.

cards.headline: Nepal PM Balendra Shah to make first India visit on Nov 22-23
cards.body: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will visit India on November 22-23, 2026, his first trip since taking charge last March, the Ministry of External Affairs announced. He will lead a 34-member delegation, hold delegation-level talks with PM Narendra Modi, and call on President Droupadi Murmu. Energy projects are expected to be inaugurated and several MoUs signed. He will also attend the Nepal-India Business Forum and lay a wreath at Rajghat.
cards.why_it_matters: Nepal is a key neighbour for India's energy, trade and connectivity ties, so this first state visit sets the tone for the new Nepali government's engagement with Delhi.
cards.key_fact: Nepal PM Balendra Shah's India state visit on November 22-23, 2026

quiz.q: When is Nepal PM Balendra Shah scheduled to visit India?
quiz.explain: The MEA announced the visit for November 22-23, 2026.

cards.headline: No change in India's Indus Waters Treaty position, says MEA
cards.body: The Ministry of External Affairs said India's position on the Indus Waters Treaty is unchanged, as Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik attended the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi. India suspended the treaty in 2025 after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said invitations were extended to all SCO members, including Pakistan, as per established practice.
cards.why_it_matters: The Indus Waters Treaty governs how India and Pakistan share river waters, so any shift in India's stance affects farmers and water supply in both countries.
cards.key_fact: India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty in 2025 after the Pahalgam attack

quiz.q: Why did India suspend the Indus Waters Treaty in 2025?
options: After the Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people
After a dispute over SCO membership
After Pakistan stopped sharing flood data
quiz.explain: The article says India suspended the treaty as a punitive measure after the April 22 Pahalgam attack.

cards.headline: India reach 486/4 on Day 3, lead New Zealand by 118
cards.body: India scored 327 runs in 86 overs on Day 3 of the first Test against New Zealand at Basin Reserve, finishing at 486/4 with a lead of 118 runs and two days left. K.L. Rahul made 136, becoming the first Indian opener to score a Test hundred in every SENA country. Devdutt Padikkal added 80, captain Shubman Gill batted fluently, and Rishabh Pant finished the day with late fireworks.
cards.why_it_matters: Rahul's SENA milestone is durable cricket general knowledge, and the big lead puts India in a strong position to push for a win in Wellington.
cards.key_fact: K.L. Rahul: first Indian opener with Test hundreds in all SENA countries

quiz.q: What record did K.L. Rahul set with his 136 at Basin Reserve?
options: First Indian opener with Test hundreds in all SENA countries
Fastest Test hundred by an Indian opener
Most Test runs by an Indian in New Zealand
First Indian to score a hundred in both innings of a Test
quiz.explain: The article says Rahul became the first Indian opener, and fifth batter overall, to score a Test hundred in each SENA country.

cards.headline: CCMB scientists identify two genes that help repair damaged nerves
cards.body: Researchers at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology in Hyderabad found that two developmental genes, NR2F1 and NR2F6, can restore the ability of damaged nerve fibres to regrow. In mice with completely injured spinal cords, activating either gene led to regrowth across the injury and better movement. Recovery appeared about five weeks after injury. The study is preclinical and published in The EMBO Journal.
cards.why_it_matters: Spinal cord injury currently has no treatment that restores lost neural connections, so a gene-based approach could eventually matter for paralysis patients in India and elsewhere.
cards.key_fact: NR2F1 and NR2F6 genes aid nerve regeneration

quiz.q: Which two genes did the CCMB team find can help damaged nerve cells regenerate?
quiz.explain: The CCMB study showed that activating NR2F1 or NR2F6 enabled severed nerve fibres to regrow in mice.

cards.headline: INCOIS expects La Niña to develop by 2027 monsoon season
cards.body: Scientists at the Hyderabad-based Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services say the strong El Niño over the Pacific is likely to remain dominant until March next year. Climate models then point to neutral conditions, followed by rising chances of La Niña developing during the 2027 Southwest Monsoon. The article does not give further figures or a final forecast on rainfall outcomes.
cards.why_it_matters: El Niño and La Niña strongly influence Indian monsoon rainfall, which shapes farm output, food prices and water availability for ordinary Indians.
cards.key_fact: INCOIS: La Niña likely by 2027 Southwest Monsoon

quiz.q: Which organisation issued the forecast on a possible La Niña by the 2027 monsoon?
quiz.explain: The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services in Hyderabad gave the forecast.

cards.headline: COP31 enters final day with fossil fuel cuts still unresolved
cards.body: Negotiators at the UN climate summit in Turkiye entered its final day without major agreements on moving away from coal, oil and gas. A goal to raise electricity's share of global energy use from about 21% to 35% by 2035 would still allow fossil fuels. The US, the largest historical polluter, was absent for a second year. Climate Action Tracker says warming progress has stalled for five years.
cards.why_it_matters: India is highly vulnerable to heat waves, floods and erratic rainfall, so the pace of global emissions cuts directly affects Indian lives and livelihoods.
cards.key_fact: COP31 held in Turkiye; 1.5°C goal set in Paris Agreement

quiz.q: Which agreement set the goal of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius?
quiz.explain: The 2015 Paris Agreement set the 1.5°C warming limit that the report says the world will overshoot.

cards.headline: Delhi AQI hits 448, November 2026 average worst on record
cards.body: Delhi's Air Quality Index reached 448 on Saturday morning, November 21, with severe smog and PM2.5 at 297 micrograms per cubic metre. PM10 was reported at 416 micrograms per cubic metre, about 9.1 times the WHO guideline. The AQI dashboard compared the exposure to smoking 11 cigarettes daily. Delhi's November 2026 average of 404 is its worst ever recorded.
cards.why_it_matters: Sustained hazardous air affects the health of millions of Delhi residents, especially children and the elderly, and prompts advisories to stay indoors and wear N95 masks.
cards.key_fact: Delhi AQI 448; November 2026 average 404, worst on record

quiz.q: What was Delhi's November 2026 average AQI, described as the worst ever recorded?
quiz.explain: The article says the November 2026 average of 404 is the worst ever recorded for the month.

cards.headline: Cyclone Akvan disrupts trains and flights in eastern India
cards.body: Cyclonic Storm Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha's Ganjam district on Friday between 10.30 and 11 am, then moved north-northwest at 55-65 kmph while weakening. The East Coast Railway cancelled 45 trains and rescheduled 29; the South Eastern Railway cancelled at least 28 express trains. Air India and IndiGo issued advisories for Bhubaneswar, Kolkata and Visakhapatnam. Mayurbhanj and Balasore are under a red warning.
cards.why_it_matters: Cyclone alerts and cancellations help protect passengers and assets, and show how coastal Odisha regularly faces storm landfalls each year.
cards.key_fact: Cyclone Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur, Ganjam district

quiz.q: Where did Cyclone Akvan make landfall?
options: Near Gopalpur in Ganjam district, Odisha
quiz.explain: Odisha minister Suresh Pujari said Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur in Ganjam district on Friday morning.

cards.headline: Core sector growth hits series-high 10.9% in October 2026
cards.body: Official data from the Ministry of Commerce and Industry show growth in the eight core industries rose to 10.9% in October 2026, up from 8.2% in September, the previous series high. Coal grew 23.05% and electricity generation 21.6%. Economists cautioned the figure was aided by a low base, as the index grew only 0.8% in October last year.
cards.why_it_matters: Core industries like coal, cement and electricity feed most other economic activity, so their output is a key early signal of how fast the wider economy is growing.
cards.key_fact: Core sector growth in October 2026: 10.9%

quiz.q: What was the growth rate of the core industrial sectors in October 2026?
quiz.explain: The Index of Core Industries showed 10.9% growth in October 2026, surpassing September's 8.2%.

cards.headline: RBI eases export declaration rules for individual service exporters
cards.body: The RBI has clarified that resident individuals exporting services need not file a separate export declaration form; providing transaction details to their authorised dealer bank will count as submission. Companies and other non-individual exporters must file the form only when a single inward remittance exceeds ₹10 lakh. The SOFTEX filing requirement with STPI has also been discontinued from 1 October.
cards.why_it_matters: Smaller freelancers and service exporters face lighter paperwork when receiving payments from overseas clients, which supports India's services exports.
cards.key_fact: EDF threshold for non-individual service exporters: ₹10 lakh

quiz.q: For non-individual service exporters, an export declaration form is required only when a single inward remittance exceeds what amount?
quiz.explain: The RBI set the threshold at ₹10 lakh or its foreign currency equivalent per inward remittance.

cards.headline: Minister asks states to complete SVAMITVA property cards by March 2027
cards.body: At a review meeting in New Delhi, Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh urged mission-mode implementation of the SVAMITVA scheme to reach 100% coverage by 31 March 2027. Launched on 24 April 2020, the scheme uses drone surveys and GIS mapping to give rural households legal property records. So far 3.28 lakh villages have been surveyed and 3.47 crore property cards issued.
cards.why_it_matters: SVAMITVA property cards give rural owners formal proof of title, which banks now accept as loan collateral, helping families borrow without informal moneylenders.
cards.key_fact: SVAMITVA scheme launched on 24 April 2020

quiz.q: In which year was the SVAMITVA scheme launched?
quiz.explain: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched SVAMITVA on 24 April 2020.

cards.headline: Supreme Court seeks Centre's reply on law for consanguineous marriages
cards.body: A Bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant issued notice to the Union government on a plea to regulate marriages between people closely related by blood. The court said it cannot regulate such marriages, as the issue falls within the legislature's domain. The notice is limited to asking the Centre to consider suitable legislation or wide publicity on the health consequences of such marriages.
cards.why_it_matters: It shows the separation of powers, where courts can nudge the legislature on social policy but not legislate or ban practices themselves.
cards.key_fact: Consanguineous marriages are regulated by the legislature, not courts

quiz.q: What did the Supreme Court say about regulating consanguineous marriages?
options: The issue falls exclusively within the legislature's domain
Only states can legislate on them
The court will frame guidelines itself
quiz.explain: The Bench said such marriages cannot be regulated by the court and the matter lies with the legislature.

cards.headline: Congress offers four-point formula on delimitation, INDIA bloc backs it
cards.body: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said his party favours resolving delimitation through consultation and proposed retaining the Lok Sabha's 543 seats, keeping the present state-wise distribution, reserving one-third (182) seats for women, and freezing all three for 25 years. He said INDIA bloc allies including the DMK share the position. Delimitation follows the ongoing Census results early next year.
cards.why_it_matters: Delimitation will redraw Lok Sabha seats after the Census, and southern states that curbed population growth fear losing relative representation.
cards.key_fact: Existing Lok Sabha strength: 543 seats

quiz.q: How many Lok Sabha seats does the Congress formula propose to retain?
quiz.explain: The Congress proposed retaining the existing strength of 543 Lok Sabha seats, with 182 reserved for women.

cards.headline: US court jails Nikhil Gupta for 235 months in Pannun murder plot
cards.body: A US federal court in New York sentenced Indian national Nikhil Gupta, 55, to 235 months in prison for his role in a murder-for-hire plot targeting Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun on American soil. Gupta had pleaded guilty earlier this year to murder-for-hire, conspiracy and money-laundering charges. Judge Victor Marrero said Gupta will face deportation proceedings after completing his term.
cards.why_it_matters: The case drew attention to alleged links between Indian officials and a plot against a US-based Sikh figure, making it significant for India-US relations and international law.
cards.key_fact: 235 months' prison term for Nikhil Gupta

quiz.q: What sentence did the US court give Nikhil Gupta?
quiz.explain: Judge Victor Marrero imposed a 235-month prison term on Gupta.

cards.headline: Botswana cheetah KOMG 3 gives birth to four cubs at Kuno
cards.body: A two-and-a-half-year-old cheetah from Botswana, KOMG 3, gave birth to four healthy cubs in the wild at Madhya Pradesh's Kuno National Park. Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav said this is the first time a cheetah from Botswana has given birth in India. It is the second recorded wild birth since Project Cheetah's reintroduction began in 2022, taking India's cheetah count to 62.
cards.why_it_matters: Project Cheetah, launched in 2022, is the world's first intercontinental translocation of the big cat, and successful wild births signal the programme's longer-term viability.
cards.key_fact: India's cheetah population now 62

quiz.q: With the four new cubs, what is India's total cheetah population?
quiz.explain: The article states the population has risen to 62, including 43 Indian-born individuals.

cards.headline: Project Cheetah turns four; India's cheetah population reaches 52
cards.body: As Project Cheetah completed four years on September 17, 2026, officials said India's cheetah population had risen to 52, including 32 cubs born in the country. The programme began when Prime Minister Narendra Modi released eight Namibian cheetahs at Kuno National Park in 2022. Forty-nine cheetahs are now at Kuno and three at Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary, both in Madhya Pradesh.
cards.why_it_matters: The cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952, so the reintroduction project's progress is a test case for large-carnivore restoration in the country.
cards.key_fact: Project Cheetah launched on September 17, 2022

quiz.q: When was Project Cheetah launched with the release of Namibian cheetahs at Kuno?
quiz.explain: PM Modi released eight Namibian cheetahs at Kuno National Park on September 17, 2022.

cards.headline: Over 1 crore HPV vaccine doses given to 14-year-old girls
cards.body: The Health Ministry said more than one crore HPV vaccine doses have been given to 14-year-old girls in under nine months, covering nearly 87% of the annual target of about 1.2 crore girls. The free, voluntary single-dose campaign was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in February 2026. Six States, including Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, have achieved 100% coverage of their targets.
cards.why_it_matters: HPV vaccination protects girls against high-risk strains linked to cervical cancer, a major cause of cancer deaths among Indian women.
cards.key_fact: Over 1 crore HPV vaccine doses in nine months

quiz.q: What percentage of the annual target did the HPV campaign cover?
quiz.explain: The Ministry said the drive covered nearly 87% of the identified annual target.

cards.headline: Health Ministry proposes to treat antimicrobials as 'New Drugs'
cards.body: The Union Health Ministry has proposed amending the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019, to bring antimicrobials under the 'New Drug' definition, citing concerns over manufacturing licences being granted without adequate scrutiny. Manufacturers would first need permission from the Central Licensing Authority. Separately, it proposed a dedicated licence for wholesale of bulk drugs, agreed by the DCC and DTAB.
cards.why_it_matters: Antimicrobial resistance is a major global public health threat, and tighter central oversight of antimicrobial manufacturing is meant to curb misuse.
cards.key_fact: New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019

quiz.q: Which rules would the Health Ministry amend to include antimicrobials as 'New Drugs'?
options: New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019
quiz.explain: The proposal seeks to amend Rule 2(1)(w)(v) of the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019.
